speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I see you are presenting with chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort; to help me understand your condition, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The relief of cramping after bowel movements and the sensation of incomplete evacuation are classic signs of irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D) or an infectious process like Campylobacter. Given your camping trip and a sick contact, was the onset of these symptoms acute immediately after the trip, or did it develop gradually?

speaker: Doctor
text: The clustering of your symptoms—urgent bowel movements, mucus, and incomplete evacuation—along with the recent contact with a sick person from your camping trip, strongly suggests an infectious etiology, possibly Campylobacter or Shigella. To confirm this, I need to see the results of your stool studies. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Culture, REQUEST TEST: Ova_and_Parasites. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CXR.
